Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: September 14, 2026 SUBJECT: Action Item: Consideration of an Amendment to the Bond Issuance Resolutions approved on April 24, 2026, and February 13, 2026 Purpose of Submittal: This request is to amend two resolutions by the Board of Trustees in conjunction with borrowing for “Utility Infrastructure – Phase III” project(s) to allow for funding to be acquired through the Rhode Island Infrastructure Bank (RIIB) or the Rhode I sland Health and Educational Building Corporation (RIHEBC).
URI is currently evaluating borrowing options through both RIIB and RIHEBC and is seeking flexibility to make the best financial decision for the university based on market conditions.
Points to Consider: The sole change to these resolutions will be the allowance of the source of funds relative to Utility Infrastructure “Utility Infrastructure – Phase III” project(s) to allow for funding to be acquired through the RIIB in addition to RIHEBC.

The two Resolutions that shall be amended were approved by the Board of Trustees April 24, 2026 (the “April Resolution”) and February 13, 2026 (the “February Resolution”).
The February Resolution allowed for reimbursement to the university for funds expended for the project, and the April Resolution allowed for the debt issuance through RIHEBC.
As a reminder to the Committee, Utility Infrastructure – Phase III is the third of a four anticipated phases of work to upgrade the University’s primary utility systems to replace infrastructure that is nearing its end of life.
Given the age of this infrastructure, the University experiences unplanned outages that affect multiple campus buildings, interrupting the academic and research programs within.
This project, which is currently ongoing, will provide a more stable campus environment through the design and construction of upgrades and component replacements to our municipal-level campus utility system.

Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the enclosed Resolution effective upon its passage to amend the April and February Resolutions to allow for funding of these projects by RIHEBC and by RIIB.
Supporting Information: See attached Resolution.

Proposed Motion of the Board: To recommend approval of the resolution amending the “April Resolution” and the “February Resolution “authorizing the borrowing through the Rhode Island Infrastructure Bank and the Rhode Island Health and Education Building Corporation for Utility Infrastructure Upgrade – Phase III as presented in the enclosed Resolution.

Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: April 13, 2026 SUBJECT: Action Item: Consideration of Bond Issuance Resolution P urpose of Submittal: This request is to approve a resolution to authorize that URI, through the Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation (RIHEBC), issue up to $42.2M in revenue bonds in fall of 2026, and to refund existing bonds if market conditions are deemed favorable.
The following projects would be supported by the new bonds issued under the university’s Education and General covenant, which means that debt service would be covered by the university’s unrestricted funds: 1.
U tility Infrastructure Upgrade – Phase III (total project cost: $9.2M) 2.
Repaving and Hardscape Improvements (total project cost: $20M) 3.

Facilities Service Sector Upgrade (total project cost: $13M) P oints to Consider: All debt issuances by State agencies must receive authorization from the state legislature, called "Kushner authorizations" after Linda Kushner, the representative who sponsored the bill requiring them.
The Kushner authorization for the Facilities Service Sector Upgrade is included in Article 4 of H7123Aaa which established the State budget for fiscal year 2023.
The Kushner authorization for the Utility Infrastructure Phase III is included in Article 4 of H7225, the budget bill which established the State budget for fiscal year 2025.
The Kushner authorization for the Repaving and Hardscape Improvements project is included in the Governor’s Recommended budget for fiscal year 2027 and is under consideration by the General Assembly.
T he first project, Facilities Service Sector Upgrade, involves work to enhance and reorganize facilities within the service sector for more efficient and effective operations, including construction of a new Lands and Grounds Building which is currently housed in a former Dairy Barn that is in very poor condition.

The s econd project, Utility Infrastructure Phase III, is the third of a four anticipated phases of work to upgrade the University’s primary utility systems to replace infrastructure that is nearing its end of life.
Given the age of this infrastructure, the University experiences unplanned outages that effect multiple campus buildings, interrupting the academic and research programs within.
This project will provide a more stable campus environment through the design and construction of upgrades and component replacements to our municipal-level campus utility system.
APPROVED BY THE BOARD ON APRIL 24, 2026

The third project, Repaving and Hardscaping, will allow URI to repave and reconstruct parking facilities, roadways, and walkways across three campuses of URI, as well as provide improvements to landscape elements.
This project will support replacing parking lost due to the new undergraduate residential buildings currently under construction as well as the extension and paving of Farmhouse Road, a critical enabling project for the Comprehensive Campus Plan.
We anticipate issuing $4.5M of the total project amount in 2026, with the remainder supported by a future bond issuance.
The University’s Series 2016A and 2016B bonds become refundable as of June 2026, and we anticipate refunding these bonds simultaneously with the new issuance - if market conditions are favorable - to reduce the University’s overall debt service on these bonds.
Approval of this resolution does not commit the university to issue these bonds, if market conditions or other factors result in unfavorable conditions to do so.

The University sought and received approval at the February meeting to allow for reimbursement of expenditures related to the Utilities Phase III project before the issuance of debt supporing the projects, so work could begin in the critical summer months of 2026.
The approved reimbursement amount was capped at $6.91M.
Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the enclosed Resolution effective April 13, 2026, to authorize the issuance of RIHEBC bonds in support of these three projects and allow for refunding of any refundable bonds to reduce overall debt service.
Supporting Information: See attached Resolution.

These tax- the issuance of tax-exempt bonds, use such bond proceeds to reimburse itself for the advanced funds, and treat such bond proceeds as being “spent" for federal tax purposes when the reimbursement is made, thus avoiding further tax compliance with respect to such funds.
To avail itself of the ability to make such reimbursement, under the applicable tax regulations, the University must declare its “official intent’ prior to making the capital expenditures expected to be reimbursed from bond proceeds.
URI is seeking this declaration of “official intent” from the Board to reimburse itself for funds related revenue bonds contemplated to be issued in Fall 2026, pending Board of Trustees approval.
These two projects would begin in summer 2026.

URI has already received Kushner authorization to issue the Utility Infrastructure Phase IHI project bond, and the Kushner for the Parking and Repaving project is included in the FY27 Governor's request and is currently under review by the General Assembly.

BACKGROUND The University of Rhode Island is seeking a dedicated and qualified vendor to provide emergency and routine utility maintenance and repair services for all underground and above -ground utility systems , excluding electrical , located on the Kingston, Narragansett Bay and W.
Alton Jones campuses .
These critical systems include steam, water (potable and non-potable), sewage, storm water, natural gas, propane and heating oil.
The Kingston campus consists of 197 buildings totaling over 4 million square feet with miles of underground utility systems.
URI owned utility systems on the Kingston campus include a central steam plant, steam and condensate distribution/return network s, Five natural gas distribution networks, sewer collection system with four sewer pump stations, potable water supply and distribution, oil and propane fuel storage tanks for heating systems and a stormwater collection system.
The 153 acre Narragansett Bay Campus consists of 41 buildings and 326,000 square feet.

Utilities include natural gas supplied by RIE and distributed by URI owned piping network, potable water provided by the town and distributed by URI owned piping network, sewer collected by URI owned piping network and sent to the town for treatment, stormwater collection sy stem and oil and propane fuel storage for heating and generators.
The W.
Alton Jones campus is a rural campus in West Greenwich, RI and composed of 30 buildings.
Utilities include three small public water systems, septic systems, propane and oil storage for heating systems.
The selected vendor must have a thorough understanding of connection and repair methods for each of these utilities and an integral understanding of each of the university’s utility systems is necessary for undertaking the scope of work described in Section B of this solicitation.
The vendor shall demonstrate troubleshooting of utility outages and methods of providing control of the utility network and temporary service.
As such, the selected vendor(s) will be required to study and understand the universi ty’s utility systems within the first 6 months of the contract’s award date.

The selected vendor(s) will be required to provide routine and emergency service for pipefitter, steamfitter and plumbing services, along with all construction equipment, excavation services and materials required to perform the necessary task/repair.
Services shall also include investigation as necessary to ensure proper repair (locating, camera work, transit level, etc).
For clarification, the University will continue to utilize the State Master Price Agreement for general plumbing (MPA #40) and steamfitter work (MPA #199) for repairs and maintenance outside of the scope of utilities.
SECTION B: SCOPE OF WORK AND REQUIREMENTS Vendors submitting proposals in response to this solicitation must demonstrate that they have the capacity, capability and qualifications to respond to emergency and non- emergency utility events and maintenance requests.
Vendors shall demonstrate and furnish the labor, materials, and equipment necessary for repairing underground and above -ground utility systems, including excavation, utility repair and site restoration services where necessary.

Utility systems covered under this service contract will incl ude steam, potable and non-potable water, natural gas, propane, heating oil, sewer and storm water infrastructure.
All materials used for maintenance and repairs to utility systems must satisfy code requirements and conform with the University’s standards for pipe and fittings.
These standards are provided in Appendix D.
Vendors shall

Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 15, 2026 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of a Contract in Excess of $5 Million: Chiller Maintenance and Repair Purpose of Submittal: The purpose of this action item is to seek Board of Trustees approval, under the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents, of a new contract for the Facilities Operations group.
This contract represents ongoing support services which are part of the current operations of the campus for service and repair to the University’s chillers and HVAC systems.
The contract for these services has not yet been awarded, but is expected to be awarded by the State to begin July 1, 2026.
This proposed contract will replace the award previously approved by the Board in November 2023 for $6M over three years.
Because this proposed contract is in the bid award determination process , no supplier is identified at this time.

Once the State is ready to award the contract to the successful bidder, we anticipate that contract value to be closer to $5.0M, but we are requesting approval for a cap of $5.50M on the contract to allow for flexibility.
The targeted $5.0M expense is less than the prior contract for similar services because certain components of the contract have been updated and certain services split out to better serve the University.
Recommendation: It is recommended that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the proposed award for the Chiller Maintenance and Repair contract, which is expected to be issued for July 1, 2026.
Points to Consider: This prior contract approved by the Board of Trustees in November of 2023 exceeded its original estimated value largely due to unanticipated emergency repairs and required equipment replacement.
To better assess the new contract, the Facilities Operations group completed a comprehensive review of the services provided and decided to split out certain components of the work to better foster competition.

To meet the HVAC and chiller maintenance and repair needs of the University th rough this new time and materials contract, the University is proposing a $5.50M cap to the spend that includes unanticipated emergencies.
The University’s Facilities Operations group continues to work with URI Purchasing to maximize contracting options for HVAC equipment replacement, as well as preventative maintenance and repair.
